claim: In current NixOS (Oct 2025), nixos-rebuild switch only restarts nixos-activation.service at the user systemd manager level, and only for users that are currently logged in
stance_target: declarative restart-on-switch for systemd.user.services does not exist for non-logged-in users; system services get restartIfChanged but user services do not
scope_conditions: NixOS, nixos-rebuild switch, systemd user services, October 2025
quoted_support: Note that nixos-rebuild switch only restarts nixos-activation.service in the user level systemd manager for users that are currently logged in.

claim: NixOS has no equivalent of the system sysinit-reactivation.target for user services; restartTriggers + requiredBy workarounds target the system-level activation target
stance_target: the user-service model lacks the restart machinery the system-service model has on switch
scope_conditions: NixOS, user services, rebuild switch semantics
quoted_support: I don’t think we have an equivalent reactivation thing for user services, other than the user service nixos-activation.service, which just runs system.userActivationScripts

claim: When the home-manager NixOS module is used, home-manager activation runs as a SYSTEM service during nixos-rebuild, not a user service, though it may set up user-level services
stance_target: home-manager as NixOS module gets system-service restart semantics for its activation, but user services it installs still rely on the user manager
quoted_support: if you’re using the home-manager NixOS module, that gets run on nixos-rebuild by a system service, not a user service, though of course that home-manager activation might setup user-level services and stuff.
